clue.text: Can see possibilities in a spirited meeting

indicators.note: possibilities are the different ways the letters could be arranged, so the words are to be rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone considers the options open at a lively get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' looks like 'lively', but it means involving spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A séance is a gathering where people try to contact the spirits of the dead, a punning sense of spirited.

clue.text: Assist talk of a gullible person

indicators.note: talk of means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

blocks.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: Help with gossip about a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: To succour someone is to give help or relief to them in time of need.

clue.text: A doctorate about one small bug

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the degree wraps round the numeral

blocks.note: taken as written
Doctor of Philosophy, the usual doctoral degree
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctoral thesis on a tiny insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a tiny sap-sucking insect such as a greenfly, and bug is a common word for insect.

clue.text: Chattered merrily while cooking richer pud

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone chatted cheerfully while making a richer dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Pud is British shorthand for pudding, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To chirrup is to chirp like a bird, and figuratively to talk in a bright, lively way.

clue.text: The children are in favour of, for example, returning to New York

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

blocks.note: pro means for, in favour of
the usual abbreviation, exempli gratia
standard abbreviation of the city or state

explanation.surface: A statement that the kids support something before heading back to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' turns round in the middle; 'returning to New York' sounds like a journey but only the abbreviation flips.
explanation.definitionFit: Progeny means a person's offspring or descendants, which collectively are their children.

clue.text: Sending letters of appointment

blocks.note: first meaning: putting mail in the post
second meaning: an assignment to a job or station

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters of appointment' looks like one phrase; break it after 'letters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posting is mailing letters, and a posting is also an assignment to a job or place, as for a diplomat or soldier.

clue.text: Oil compound used by the whole industry

indicators.note: used by suggests the letters are employed inside the words that follow, sitting within them

blocks.note: spanning the end of whole and the start of industry

explanation.surface: A chemical in oil that every manufacturer employs.
explanation.definitionFit: Olein is a glyceride of oleic acid, a main constituent of many oils and fats.

clue.text: Dance for any number? On the contrary!

blocks.note: surface reading: a dance anyone may join, however many people turn up
setter's reading: it is a dance for a fixed number, and swapping 'some' and 'eight' gives the name

explanation.walkthrough: A Scottish reel danced by exactly eight people; 'some eight' turned around is the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome is a lively Scottish reel for eight dancers, so it is a dance for a set number.

clue.text: Proceeds after you initially slide off

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
off means gone wrong, so the letters of the word before it are scrambled
after places the rearranged letters following the single letter

blocks.note: the first letter
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Money comes in once you first slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proceeds' could be the verb 'goes on', but here it is the noun, the money a sale brings in.
explanation.definitionFit: Yields are returns or profits from an investment, which is what proceeds are.

clue.text: Make bubbly to a European scale

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for European
a rate is a scale of charges or payment

explanation.surface: Fizz something up to a standard used across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To aerate a liquid is to charge it with air or gas, so it becomes fizzy.

clue.text: She only partly succeeds

blocks.note: surface reading: a woman who manages only some success
setter's reading: succeeds in the sense of inheriting, but sharing the inheritance with another person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds' means 'follows as heir', not 'does well'; a joint female heir inherits only a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheiress is a woman who inherits jointly with others, so she takes over only part of an estate.

clue.text: Standard coin once

blocks.note: first meaning: the emblem carried at the head of a Roman legion
second meaning: a former United States ten-dollar gold coin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard coin' reads like ordinary currency; split it, and standard means a flag or banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman legions marched behind an eagle emblem as their banner, and the American ten-dollar gold piece was also called by that bird's name.

clue.text: Bishop leaves garden bed in a neat state

indicators.note: when the churchman leaves he is taken out of the word that follows

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a border is a strip of flower bed along a garden's edge

explanation.surface: A clergyman walks away from a flower bed that has been tidied.
explanation.walkthrough: BORDER with its B removed gives ORDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Order is a condition of tidiness in which everything is arranged properly, the opposite of mess.

clue.text: Put off by a story Dante edited

indicators.note: an edited text has been reworked, so the poet's name is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
a story can be a fib, an untruth
the Italian poet's name used as fodder

explanation.surface: A reader finds a tale by Dante, revised by an editor, offputting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' here is a fib, not a tale; DANTE rearranged supplies the last five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alienated is to be estranged or made unsympathetic, much as being put off turns someone away.

clue.text: Further episode of ill-feeling

blocks.note: surface reading: another bout of resentment or animosity
setter's reading: feeling ill, a fresh attack of sickness after recovery seemed under way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' usually means bad blood between people; read literally it is feeling ill again.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a deterioration after partial recovery, when the patient falls sick once more.

clue.text: Praising old archbishop, a Conservative

blocks.note: William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
taken as written
Tory is the familiar name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Speaking well of a former churchman who was a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Laud is also a word for praise, which suits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudatory means expressing praise or commendation, an adjective formed like praising.

clue.text: Monstrous woman turning the drink back on

indicators.note: turning the drink round, and back, both say it is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: grog is rum diluted with water, a sailor's drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A frightening woman who switches the drink back on, like a tap.
explanation.walkthrough: GROG reversed gives GORG, then ON. Grog is rum mixed with water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gorgons of Greek myth were snake-haired female monsters, and the word is still used for a fearsome woman.

clue.text: Get back papers on race disturbances

indicators.note: disturbances are upsets and disorder, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order
on places the stationery after the rearranged letters, attached to them

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Newspapers covering race riots recover something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests newspapers, but it is the stationer's quantity of sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: To reacquire something is to obtain it again after losing it, which is getting it back.

clue.text: Means of steering Democrat into being less polite

indicators.note: the party initial goes into the middle of the comparative adjective

blocks.note: comparative of rude
standard abbreviation of Democrat

explanation.surface: A tactic for nudging a politician from the Democratic party into rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder is the hinged blade at a boat's stern used to steer it.

clue.text: Instructions for making about a hundred mince pies

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the letters of the word after it are cut up and rearranged

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Directions for baking roughly a hundred mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pies' looks like Christmas pastries, but 'mince' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes are sets of directions telling a cook how to prepare a dish.

clue.text: Expert made off into the world of scholarship

indicators.note: food gone off has turned bad, so these letters are spoiled into a new order
the rearranged letters are put inside the word for an expert

blocks.note: an ace is someone highly skilled
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A specialist went off to academic life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made off' reads as 'fled', but 'off' is the anagram signal and MADE the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic community and environment, the sphere of universities and learning.

clue.text: A naval agreement

blocks.note: surface reading: a treaty between navies
setter's reading: a sailor's spoken assent to an order

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a pact between fleets; it is the reply a seaman gives to an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors acknowledge an order with this double yes, the traditional naval response meaning understood and will comply.

clue.text: Slight bulge in column of building as inset

indicators.note: building means constructing, so the letters are put together in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An architectural feature: a column swelling slightly, as if set into a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' seems part of the architecture; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Entasis is the slight convex curve given to a column's shaft to correct the illusion of concavity.

clue.text: Conveyance of property to the French

blocks.note: land is real property
au is French for 'to the' before a masculine noun

explanation.surface: A legal transfer of property to French buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conveyance of property' is the lawyer's term for transferring ownership, but conveyance here means a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, and conveyance is an old word for a vehicle.

clue.text: Snowdrop found in the mountains

blocks.note: surface reading: a small white spring flower growing on high slopes
setter's reading: a drop, or fall, of snow down a mountainside

explanation.walkthrough: The flower is a red herring: split 'Snowdrop' into snow plus drop, a mass of snow falling.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding suddenly down a mountain slope.

clue.text: Helps when accepting wager

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for when holds the stake inside it

blocks.note: as means when, at the time that
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Someone lends a hand by agreeing to a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Abetting, as in 'aiding and abetting', fits a gambling accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Leave nothing inside the ring

indicators.note: the zero shape goes inside the word for leaving

blocks.note: to quit is to leave
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave nothing in a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A quoit is a ring of rope or metal thrown at a peg in the game of quoits.

clue.text: It's said you love scrambled egg

indicators.note: it's said means the next word is taken by its sound, a single letter
scrambled eggs are mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like this pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reportedly you are fond of scrambled egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled egg' seems a dish, but 'scrambled' acts on the letters before it and 'egg' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovule is a small or unfertilised egg cell, from the Latin diminutive of ovum.

clue.text: Forced daughter to overwork

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or manipulate it, so the letters before it are reshaped

blocks.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
the first half of this word is the fodder; its second half is the signal to rearrange it

explanation.surface: A parent forced their daughter to work too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwork' must be split into 'over' plus 'work': the second half is the anagram signal for the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Drove is the past tense of drive, which can mean compelled or pushed someone into acting.

clue.text: Builds bodies

blocks.note: first meaning: a person's builds, their bodily frames
second meaning: the shape and form of human bodies

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a verb phrase, someone constructing bodies; both words are plural nouns here.
explanation.definitionFit: Physique means body type, so plural physiques are builds or bodily forms such as muscular or slender frames.

clue.text: Old Greek sailor, deviously sly, takes drugs outside

indicators.note: acting deviously means taking a crooked path, so the little word is twisted
the drug-taking word goes outside the rearranged letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: to use is slang for taking illegal drugs
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A cunning ancient Greek seafarer is a drug user.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses is the Latin name of Odysseus, famous for his cunning, so 'sly' suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses, called Odysseus by the Greeks, is the hero who spent ten years sailing home from Troy.

clue.text: Holiday hideaway

blocks.note: first meaning: a break, as when Parliament or a court is not sitting
second meaning: an alcove or secret, remote corner

explanation.surface: A secluded spot for a vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both a period when business is suspended and a sheltered nook set back in a wall.
